fields.title: A tool record's versions contain what this repository pins
fields.evidence: The `tool` job's log on the pull request, under the step "Run kac.core unit tests".

sections.What it checks:
* [std-CONFIG.PIN](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/5fda7bc7c4a11c9966435bb0f1421a0a0dbd5ca2/examples/dog-fooding/standards/configuration.md#pin-a-pin-names-an-exact-version) says "An `approved` or `trial` tool record's `versions` **MUST** contain each version this
  repository pins its package at".
sections.How it works:
`ToolPinTests` in `tooling/kac.tests` reads every `approved` or `trial` tool record in this corpus that has `packages`. `RepositoryPins` finds each package's pins in these files:

| Package URL              | Pinned in                                                                    |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `pkg:nuget/...`          | a `PackageReference` in a project under `tooling/`                           |
| `pkg:pypi/...`           | a line in `docs/requirements.txt` or `.github/requirements.txt`              |
| `pkg:generic/dotnet-sdk` | `global.json`, and the SDK version in each starter pipeline                  |
| `pkg:github/...`         | a `uses:` line in a workflow, by the version in the comment after its commit |
| `pkg:golang/...`         | a `go install` line in a workflow                                            |

The workflows it reads are those under `.github/workflows/` and `template/.github/workflows/`. For each package it does three things:

* It fails where a pin falls outside `versions`. A range ending `.x`, such as `7.x`, contains every version under that
  prefix. Any other value is one exact version, such as `10.0.403`.
* It fails where `versions` is absent and something pins the package.
* It fails where `versions` is present and nothing pins the package.

The `tool` job runs it under `dotnet test --project tooling/kac.tests` on every pull request, Dependabot's included. It reads the files as they stand, so it needs no base branch.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
It proves the record's `versions` field, and nothing in the record's body. A body naming the old version passes, so a reviewer still reads the prose of a record whose pin moved.

It reads the pins listed above and no others. A package pinned anywhere else, such as a new manifest or a container image, passes unread until `RepositoryPins` learns the file. A package nothing pins and whose record gives no `versions` passes, as `tol-claude-code-cli` and `tol-gh` do.

It reads this repository alone. `drift-against-manifests` would compare the register with every repository in the estate, and it is declared and does not run.
